summary: AE/SE walkthrough of Redwood Hosted API for chat/text generation. Demo covered streaming responses, core request parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retry strategies and idempotency keys, SDK vs curl examples, and basics of observability. Customer interested in latency/cost tradeoffs and compliance docs. Agreed to share pricing, SDK snippets, and run a benchmark POC.
transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, joined by Jon, our SE. Quick intros? 
00:06 Alex Martinez: Alex here, head of ML at Brightwell, Priya's also on. We're looking at hosted options for chat generation. 
00:12 Jon Park: Great, we'll do a quick demo of the hosted API, focusing on chat/text basics — streaming, parameters, and how retries should work. 
00:25 Maya Chen: agenda is short 30, 45 min, and then next steps. 
01:02 Jon Park: so first thing — streaming. With Redwood hosted API we support chunked streaming over HTTP and SDK streaming. You'll get partial tokens as they are generated, which helps UX for chat apps. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"Write a greeting","stream":true}' 
01:45 Alex Martinez: does the streaming use SSE or plain chunked? we have some proxies that don't like SSE. 
01:50 Jon Park: good q; we support HTTP chunked and SSE in SDK layers, so you can pick. If you're behind proxies chunked is usually safer. 
02:18 Priya Singh: what's the latency like for short prompts, say 30 tokens? 
02:25 Jon Park: for hosted our p50 is typically 80–120ms for small models on short contexts, p95 ~400ms depending on load; we include token-level latency in the Console so you can break down costs vs latency. note: numbers vary by model variant and region. 
03:10 Alex Martinez: how do retries work? say a 503 happens mid-generation. 
03:18 Jon Park: we advise an idempotency key per user request so retries don't double-charge or double-generate. For streaming there's an approach: use a request-level idempotency key for non-streaming; for streaming we recommend either re-request with last-confirmed token index or fall back to non-streamed replay. The SDK exposes helpers. 
04:02 Maya Chen: common pattern is short exponential backoff with jitter, and our SDK provides a RetryPolicy you can configure — retry on transient 429/503 but not on 4xx client errors. 
04:28 Priya Singh: do you usually recommend server-side or client-side retries? 
04:31 Jon Park: server-side is safer if you want single control plane; but client-side can improve perceived latency if you detect network issues quickly. We usually do both: SDK does client retry with idempotency while backend does safe retries. 
05:00 Alex Martinez: about parameters — temperature, top_p, max_tokens — any tips? 
05:08 Jon Park: temperature tunes randomness; 0.0 for deterministic, 0.7 for more creative. top_p is nucleus sampling; you can usually tune one of them. max_tokens limits generation length; token counting uses byte-pair tokens, we show estimated token counts in Console. 
05:40 Priya Singh: does Redwood do automatic token budgeting or cost control? 
05:45 Maya Chen: we have per-route quotas and cost analytics; you can configure max tokens per request and enforce rate limits per API key. Also caching of common prefixes reduces cost for repeated queries. 
06:12 Alex Martinez: show us an SDK snippet for streaming? 
06:20 Jon Park: (shares screen) here's node example — client.stream({model:'redwood-1', input:'Summarize this', temperature:0.2, stream:true}).on('data', chunk=>...)
06:48 Alex Martinez: ok nice. any pitfalls with concurrency and KV cache? 
06:52 Jon Park: KV cache is internal; concurrency matters if you do long-lived contexts — we handle per-session KV cache. Watch memory if you pin huge contexts. 
07:18 Priya Singh: security — SOC2, SSO, data retention — do you keep transcripts? 
07:25 Maya Chen: Redwood is SOC2 compliant, supports SCIM and SAML SSO, and for hosted we retain logs per customer policy; you can opt for short retention or choose Dedicated/Private for strict control. we'll share the security pack after. 
08:00 Alex Martinez: any limits on streaming token rates? we have bursty spikes. 
08:08 Jon Park: we surface rate limits; for bursty we recommend reserved Dedicated capacity or burst policies. Hosted supports burst within quota but for heavy steady traffic Dedicated is better economically. 
09:10 Alex Martinez: cost question — if we lower temperature does cost change? 
09:14 Jon Park: cost is per output token + input tokens (and compute tiers). temperature doesn't change token count unless it causes longer outputs. quantization and batching also reduce unit cost. 
10:00 Maya Chen: quick demo of retries: (replays simulated failure) you can re-call with same idempotency key and our backend dedups; here's an example header: Idempotency-Key: xxxxxx and we attach metadata. 
11:00 Priya Singh: and for function/tool calling? 
11:05 Jon Park: supported — you can send structured function specs and the model will respond with a function call object; we stream that too. 
12:30 Alex Martinez: what about observability in Console? 
12:35 Jon Park: per-route latency histograms, token usage, per-model breakdown, traces for slow requests and error traces. We can also export logs to your SIEM. 
14:00 Alex Martinez: can we do a POC to benchmark latency/cost? 
14:05 Maya Chen: absolutely. typical POC is a 1–2 week benchmark with sample prompts and traffic, we run a char token-level comparison and share a spreadsheet. 
14:30 Alex Martinez: timeline wanting this in prod in Q2, are there any enterprise contracts? 
14:40 Maya Chen: we'll put together Dedicated pricing if needed; hosted is pay-as-you-go. For enterprise we do annual Reserved capacity. 
15:20 Priya Singh: support for VPC peering or private deploy? 
15:25 Jon Park: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem; we can discuss architecture if you have strict network requirements. 
16:00 Alex Martinez: ok let's recap next steps. 
16:05 Maya Chen: we'll send pricing and the security pack, Jon will share SDK snippets and retry policy, Alex will send sample prompts and traffic. schedule follow-up for a POC kickoff. 
16:20 Alex Martinez: thanks, that was helpful. 
16:25 Maya Chen: awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up. 
[Transcript paused — Fireflies truncated after 45 minutes]
